phase_commits.subject: Phase 149O.2: HATP Hardware Provider + Human-Presence Implementation (Wave 5)

recommended_next_phase: 149O.3 -- HATP Hardware Provider Independent Verification: independently attack the hardware-backed-key property claim, fresh-touch-per-operation enforcement, provider-profile binding, credential binding, the (currently absent) attestation path, payload byte-exactness, replay across every named dimension, test-provider isolation, optional-dependency behavior, and the operational-readiness hard ceiling, mirroring 149O.1J's rigor applied to Wave 4.
summary: Phase 149O.2 -- HATP Hardware Provider + Human-Presence Implementation (Wave 5): implemented a real HATP_HARDWARE_PROVIDER_V1-conformant hardware-provider layer per docs/PHASE_149O_1D_HUMAN_APPROVAL_TRUSTED_PROVENANCE_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md's Wave-5 section, read directly this phase, and against HATP-001 v1.0 (HATP-REQ-016..025, HATP-REQ-076), also read directly. Real FIDO2 provider (src/pcae/core/hatp_fido2_provider.py): independently confirmed against the installed fido2==1.2.0 library's own source that WebAuthn getAssertion signs authenticatorData || SHA-256(clientDataJSON), where clientDataJSON embeds a caller-supplied challenge (fido2.webauthn.CollectedClientData.create); this module binds sha256(canonicalize_hatp_proof_payload(proof)) as that challenge -- a genuine, byte-exact binding satisfying HATP-REQ-020's demonstration requirement, independently verified by tamper/replay tests (wrong payload, wrong credential, presence-from-operation-A-cannot-satisfy-B). Human presence mapped to AuthenticatorData.FLAG.UP (WebAuthn User Present), read via is_user_present(), re-checked fresh on every getAssertion call, never cached (HATP-REQ-016/017). Non-exportable key: CTAP2 authenticators never expose the private key over any documented command; request_signature() has no code path accepting or constructing one -- signing happens only via a real Ctap2.get_assertion call against an enumerated HID device. Verification uses real ECDSA via cryptography/fido2.cose (ES256/COSE), checked against a new, separate, protected, read-only hardware-credential registry (src/pcae/core/hatp_hardware_credentials.py) that supplies public-key material independent of the proof itself (HATP-REQ-019(e)/025) -- this registry deliberately does not import or modify hatp_bootstrap.py (Wave 2 stays untouched), duplicating (not importing) its fixed-platform-path/symlink-rejection/duplicate-JSON-key-rejection discipline, and exposes no enroll/grant/revoke/rotate production API, mirroring HATPTrustStore's own read-only discipline. PIV fallback (src/pcae/core/hatp_piv_provider.py) is structurally defined but unconditionally reports/raises unavailable in this environment: the FIDO2 spike succeeded, so PIV was not required by 149O.1D plan Section23's own conditional wording, and no PKCS#11/smart-card dependency exists in this codebase or environment -- documented as NOT_CONFORMANT (this phase), never silently accepted as compliant. Wave-5 abstraction layer added to src/pcae/core/hatp_providers.py: HATP_HARDWARE_PROVIDER_V1 constant, HardwareProviderCapabilities/HardwareProviderConformance, ProviderAssertion, HATPHardwareSigner Protocol (production signing interface, kept separate from the existing Wave-4-frozen HATPProofVerifierProvider verification interface), discover_hardware_providers() (availability facts only, never trust), and create_production_hardware_provider() (closed allowlist, FIDO2-primary/PIV-explicit-fallback, never resolves TestHATPProofVerifierProvider -- independently confirmed by source inspection with docstrings/comments stripped). Evidence serialization is a strict, closed, versioned JSON schema (unknown fields/missing fields/unknown version/duplicate JSON keys/non-JSON garbage all fail closed to signature_valid=False, never raise, matching the existing Wave-4-frozen provider-interface contract exactly). New optional dependency extra pcae-harness[hatp-hardware] (fido2>=1.1,<2, cryptography>=42,<45, verified compatible with requires-python>=3.9 under this repo's own .venv, Python 3.9.6); zero hard import of either library exists in hatp_providers.py or hatp_hardware_credentials.py -- only hatp_fido2_provider.py imports them, lazily, only from inside discover_hardware_providers()/create_production_hardware_provider(); a missing dependency reports library_installed=False rather than crashing ordinary PCAE import/use. New test suite tests/test_phase_149o_2_hatp_hardware_provider_implementation.py (62 passed, 1 hardware-required test skipped) uses real WebAuthn/CTAP2 data structures and real ECDSA cryptography signed with a test-only, never-enrolled, in-memory key -- this methodology caught and fixed a real bug during development (AuthenticatorData.is_user_present is a method, not a property; an early draft's unconditional-truthy access was caught immediately by a deterministic round-trip test asserting presence is False for a UP-unset assertion, not by a mock). This development machine has zero attached FIDO2/PIV hardware, independently confirmed via discover_hardware_providers() and system_profiler; the test suite honestly reports this rather than fabricating a passing hardware test. Device attestation (Root 2A) was intentionally left unimplemented this phase -- attestation_valid remains always None (Wave-4's own existing Optional-typed contract treats this as non-blocking), capabilities().hatp_conformant reports CONFORMANT_WITH_NON_BLOCKING_LIMITATIONS for FIDO2 and NOT_CONFORMANT for PIV. Wave-4's inspect_hatp_verification_substrate_readiness function was read but left completely unmodified this phase -- operational stays permanently False even with the FIDO2 library installed and a credential enrolled in a test registry, independently re-tested. Full end-to-end integration through the real (unmodified) Wave-4 verifier verify_hatp_proof, using Fido2HardwareProvider as the provider (not the deterministic TestHATPProofVerifierProvider), was exercised for VALID, REVOKED_SIGNER, WRONG_REPOSITORY, WRONG_DEPLOYMENT, and USER_PRESENCE_NOT_PROVEN outcomes. Two pre-existing diff-scope guard tests (149O.1E's and 149O.1G's own test_only_expected_production_files_changed) were widened for this phase's three new files, mirroring this project's own documented allowed-file-widening precedent from 149O.1G's and 149O.1I's prior entries. Regression, all actually re-run this phase (not assumed): Wave-4 own suite 59/59 passed, exact match; Wave-1/2 40 passed; combined -k 'hatp or 149o_1 or 149o_2' selection 1376 passed / 3 skipped / 91 failed, independently confirmed identical (same exact failure set) on unmodified main via git stash, all pre-existing and environment/timezone-dependent, unrelated to this phase; report-trust 186 passed / 1 failed, confirmed identical on unmodified main (a stateful test interacting with live .pcae/ state); Permission Broker suites 978 passed / 1 failed, the same pre-existing false-positive from hatp_bootstrap.py's own docstring prose 149O.1I/149O.1J already recorded; RAE canonical-provenance suite 1 passed / 16 failed, confirmed identical on unmodified main via git stash (the split differs from 149O.1J's recorded 4/13, an environment-dependent discrepancy not investigated per the governing instruction not to repair B-149O-1..4, which remain OPEN); Fast Green (-m fast_green -n auto) 4652 passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed, exactly baseline 4590 plus this phase's 62 new tests; test_agent.py (single-process, per 149O.1J's documented xdist-stall workaround) 4236 passed, 0 failed, exact match to 149O.1J's own claim, with zero Wave-5 module symbol referenced by agent.py or commands/agent.py, independently re-confirmed. Wrote docs/PHASE_149O_2_HATP_HARDWARE_PROVIDER_IMPLEMENTATION.md covering initial state, Wave-5 requirement reconstruction, the HATP_HARDWARE_PROVIDER_V1 contract reconstruction, the FIDO2-primary/PIV-fallback spike result and rationale, Root-1 mapping, the capability matrix, the exact signed-byte source, credential identity, human-presence mechanism, attestation semantics, provider discovery, dependency strategy, failure behavior, evidence serialization, the protected credential registry, test-provider/software-key containment, real-device test status, the substrate-readiness hard ceiling, full regression results, findings, two disclosed development-time bug corrections, the Wave-5 implementation verdict, HATP production readiness, and the recommended next phase. HATP WAVE 5 HARDWARE PROVIDER IMPLEMENTED -- READY FOR INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION. HATP PRODUCTION REMAINS NOT READY (still absent: device attestation, Class-B OS deployment provisioning, RAE/HATP production integration, AG3/AG5 Permission Broker wiring, approval_present=True derivation). Recommended next phase: 149O.3 (HATP Hardware Provider Independent Verification).

validation_results.name: fido2_spike_result
validation_results.result: Confirmed directly against installed fido2==1.2.0 source: AssertionResponse.verify() computes public_key.verify(auth_data + client_param, signature) where client_param = sha256(clientDataJSON); CollectedClientData.create() accepts an arbitrary caller-supplied challenge embedded into clientDataJSON. sha256(canonical_payload) bound as that challenge -- genuine byte-exact binding, independently exercised by tamper/replay tests. Spike SUCCEEDED; PIV fallback not required to reach conformance this phase.

validation_results.name: real_cryptography_round_trip
validation_results.result: Test-only EC P-256 key (never enrolled into any production store) used to build real WebAuthn/CTAP2-shaped assertions, verified via cryptography+fido2.cose against Fido2HardwareProvider.verify(). Valid case, wrong-payload, wrong-credential (different key), missing-presence, unknown-credential, revoked-credential, wrong-provider-profile all independently exercised with real signatures, not mocked outcomes. A genuine bug (is_user_present accessed as a property instead of called as a method, always truthy) was caught by this exact methodology and fixed before any other test was written against it.

validation_results.name: presence_mapping_up_not_uv
validation_results.result: human_presence_proven derived from AuthenticatorData.FLAG.UP (is_user_present()) only, never UV -- HATP-001's text requires 'human-presence', not 'user verification'/biometric; UP re-checked fresh on every assertion, never cached across operations, independently tested (test_presence_from_operation_a_cannot_satisfy_operation_b).
